reason: The cited evidence shows that twinning enhances strength–ductility in CrCoNi (E1, E2) and that SFE reduction increases twinning in CoCrFeMnNi (E3), but none of the passages directly support the key premise that Co removal lowers SFE in the FeNiCrMn system or that this leads to increased twinning under dynamic conditions.
premises: Co removal lowers the stacking fault energy (SFE) of the FeNiCrMn alloy relative to CoCrFeMnNi
Lower SFE increases deformation twinning activity under dynamic loading
Enhanced twinning delays dislocation accumulation and necking
This mechanism preserves strength–ductility balance across temperatures and strain rates
